A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 35 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, figures and notation table support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original synthetic sparse-recovery experiments. Appendix F and Figures 2–3 report additional meta-training results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original sparse-recovery experiments in Section 6 and the additional meta-training results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The LISTA-VM procedure, Transformer construction, soft-thresholding component and read-out functions in Section 4 and Appendix C are unchanged. Correcting 'perception' to 'perceptron' does not change the model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic noiseless sparse-recovery tasks, including fixed and varying measurement matrices, restricted support and different context lengths.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ISTA, FISTA, LISTA, LISTA-CP and ALISTA. The meta-trained LISTA and LISTA-CP comparisons in Figure 1 and Appendix F are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same data generation, losses, model configurations and training budgets, including dimension 20, sparsity 3, 12 layers or iterations, 340 baseline epochs and 10^6 Transformer epochs. Appendix F's evaluation procedure is unchanged.

E4.justification: The support-constraint study, comparison of read-out functions and Appendix F's analysis of meta-training trajectories are retained without added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Run and seed disclosures and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same original curves and smoothed curves with window size 5.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 and their accompanying findings are unchanged. For example, Appendix F reports prediction errors around 3 for meta-trained LISTA/LISTA-CP and around 0.68 for LISTA-VM in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions, Assumption 1, Theorems 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2, and the derivations and proofs in Appendices C–E are unchanged. Reworded appendix references do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about Transformers implementing L2O, linear convergence, generalization across measurement matrices and context lengths, and exploitation of support structure.

C2.justification: Remarks 1–5 retain the same interpretations of matrix adaptation, curvature information, support structure and read-out behavior. The boundedness and noiseless-analysis qualifications are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and training disclosures are unchanged, including embedding dimensions, attention-head counts, the 24 GB RTX A5000 GPU and approximate 8-hour and 12-hour training times. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. Changing 'Appendix A' to 'Section A' introduces no related-work content.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects 'multi-layer perception' to 'multi-layer perceptron'. Nine cross-references replace 'Appendix' with 'Section', and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and the Appendix B notation table retain the same graphics, captions, labels, axes, legends and placement. The page organization and display layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes a terminology correction and updates cross-reference wording and the version stamp. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence, proofs and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so these small editorial edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
